info.text:
Imports cost 8.1% more than a year ago.
U.S. import prices rose 8.1% from Sept 2025 to Sept 2026, the biggest 12-month jump since July 2022 (BLS, Oct 16, 2026).
Fuel imports: +34.5% in a year. Nonfuel imports: +6.0%, the most since April 2022.
Imported capital goods, including computers and chips, are up 8.4%, with demand tied to AI investment.
Import prices measure what U.S. buyers pay foreign sellers, before tariffs.
Sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
News and education, not financial advice.
